name: Structure follows strategy
idea: A research summary states that the work uses four historical case studies to argue that a company's structure follows its strategy. In its account, many companies adopted the multi-divisional form independently because the strategy they had taken up required it; the firms studied created that form to run large diversified companies more efficiently than a simple holding company.
suggests: Look at whether a company's organisation changed when its strategy did, for example whether a move into new products or markets came with new divisions, and whether its present structure would hold back its next strategic move.
limits: The summary states that the work presents the forms as a product of a particular strategic context, tied to technological and market changes such as the growth of transport and communication networks.
competing_idea: An open textbook adds that the influence also runs the other way: the structure a firm chooses will shape its strategy later on, and once in place, a structure limits the strategic moves the firm can make next.
questions: Has the company's strategy changed lately, for example by moving into new products or markets, and has its organisation changed with it?
Does its structure, such as divisions each run on their own results, fit the strategy it now pursues?
Would the present structure make the next strategic move slow or hard?
